To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neuraminidases enhance cell-cell fusion and RSV infection, and this enhancement is mediated by the F glycoprotien and is not due to removal of negative charges.
neuraminidases enhance RSV fusion and infection, but only if they are added to the virions or to the cells expressing the viral glyco- proteins.
neuraminidases enhance RSV fusion and infection by a novel mechanism that is distinct from the known mechanism for neuraminidases in other viral systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of SA in the infection and fusion process of respiratory syncytical virus.
the role of sialic acid in RSV infection.
the role of SA in viral fusion and infectivity and the mechanism by which neuraminidase enhances fusion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neuraminidases enhance fusion and infection by removing SA from the surface of the virions.
the SA on the virions or on the infected cells is a barrier to fusion, and that the SA on virions or on infected cells can be removed by the neuraminidases, which in turn increases fusion.
the removal of the negatively-charged SA from RSV virions or infected cells enhances fusion and infection by RSV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neuraminidases are able to enhance RSV infectivity by enhancing cell-cell fusion, but only when the neuraminidases can gain access to the target cell membrane.
removal of SA from RSV-infected or virions by neuraminidase enhances fusion between cells expressing the viral glycopeptides.
neuraminidases are not only involved in virus release and cell entry, but can also enhance cell-cell fusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SA moiety on RSV-infected host cells is a negative regulator of fusion and infectivity, possibly by sterically hindering the fusion process.
neuraminidases enhance infection of cells with RSV by increasing the efficiency of cell-cell fusion.
neuraminidases are not simply removing a negative charge but rather are removing a molecule that is involved in a fusion-inhibitory process.
